author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Restore missing fog and haze with a software-rendered reference
summary: Choose two depth-rich scenes, compare native hardware APIs with a short software reference, increase framebuffer or blending accuracy minimally, and verify that restored haze does not cover the HUD or flatten scene depth.
heroAlt: PCSX2 graphics comparison capture of an atmospheric outdoor scene

blocks.text: Use depth landmarks to measure atmospheric loss

Fog is not just a gray overlay. It usually changes with distance, preserves nearby objects, blends toward a scene color, and can interact with sky or particles. Select a view with near, middle, and far landmarks, then a second scene using smoke or interior haze. Record weather and mission state so legitimate variation is not mistaken for missing output.
Raising television brightness can reveal dark distant geometry but cannot restore the game's depth-dependent fog equation. Validate the effect in direct screenshots before touching the display chain.

items: An in-game save with stable weather and three visible depth landmarks.
A second scene with a different fog color or density.
Native internal resolution and shaders disabled.
Automatic blending plus active renderer and driver documented.
Performance evidence from the effects-heavy scene.

blocks.text: Find where the fog pass disappears

items: 1. Cold-boot the first scene and capture near, middle, and far landmark contrast.
2. Compare the supported hardware APIs while keeping resolution, blending, and driver unchanged.
3. Use software rendering briefly to record the intended depth gradient and HUD composition.
4. Switch back to the hardware renderer that completed the baseline, then test the next blending-accuracy level in the same fog-heavy scene.
5. Stop at the first tier that restores the gradient; do not continue toward maximum by habit.
6. Check that sky, water, particles, and the HUD remain in the correct order.
7. Replay the second atmospheric scene to prove the change is not tuned to one fog color.
8. Measure sustained speed after warm-up and save the value only for this title.

blocks.text: Atmospheric passes may blend with existing color or depth-derived information, so a hardware shortcut can omit or mis-order them. The software frame distinguishes a missing pass from a deliberately clear scene. Two different fog conditions reveal a false fix that merely darkens or tints the entire output.
The restored effect should carry scene depth rather than behave like a screen filter.

items: Near objects remain clear while distant landmarks fade progressively.
HUD and subtitles are not tinted or hidden by world fog.
Sky and water meet the haze without a hard rectangular seam.
Both reference scenes survive cold boot with the same profile.
Warm-session performance remains acceptable for gameplay.

blocks.text: Fog tests that do not prove a fix

items: The whole image becomes uniformly gray: reject the tier or shader combination.
Fog appears only after loading an emulator state: reproduce from the in-game save.
Software output also lacks the documented effect: verify game state, region, and image.
Only the custom driver loses haze: restore system driver and isolate the driver regression.

blocks.text: Return blending to Automatic, reselect the prior hardware API and system driver, and cold-boot both saved scenes. Remove any display tint or shader introduced during comparison so the original missing-fog evidence remains visible and reproducible.

Serial, executable revision, mission progress, and randomized weather can change the intended scene. A setting validated on one region should not be copied to another without repeating the same depth-landmark test.
